title: Knowledge Check 2: Lessons 6–10
description: Pooled check over Lessons 6–10 of the Hermes Consultant Intermediate series. Score 80% or higher to unlock the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Estimating Multi-Week Engagements: Beyond the 30-45 Minute Task”, what is the central focus?
options: The 30-45 minute task is the unit of execution, not the unit of estimation. This lesson teaches you to size a real multi-week delivery: how to break a large eng…
A history of the technology and its vendors
A review of unrelated productivity tools
A summary of corporate policy rules
questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: The 30-45 minute task is the unit of execution, not the unit of estimation. This lesson teaches you to size a real multi-week delivery: how to break a large engagement into estimable pieces, why you estimate the critical path and not the total, how to put the constraints and reviews from Lesson 5 into the number, and how to keep an estimate honest when the environment reveals surprises.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: You learned in the early lessons to scope every piece of work small enough that an agent, or a person, can execute it in a bounded window and report a clean result.
The 30-45 minute task is the unit of execution.
That discipline is correct, and it is what makes a delivery run without stalling.
But it produces a dangerous instinct when you face a multi-week engagement: the instinct to estimate the engagement the same way you estimate a task, by adding up the pieces.
questions.explanation: The 30-45 minute task is the unit of execution.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Running a Full Engagement”, what is the central focus?
options: Turning the five-phase lifecycle into a week-by-week plan: mapping discover, design, implement, handover, and support onto a real calendar, with gates, buffers,…
A history of the technology and its vendors

A summary of corporate policy rules
questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: Turning the five-phase lifecycle into a week-by-week plan: mapping discover, design, implement, handover, and support onto a real calendar, with gates, buffers, and the scheduling realities that kill engagements.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: You will learn how to map the five phases onto a real week-by-week plan, how to set gates that hold, how much buffer to carry, and where the schedule quietly goes wrong on real engagements.
Level 1 gave you the container: five phases, discover, design, implement, handover, support, each with a product and an exit test.
The working example is a six-week Hermes Agent delivery, and the skill transfers to any tool you ever run.
It tells you what has to happen, not when, not how long each part gets, and not how to keep a multi-week engagement alive while it runs.
questions.explanation: Level 1 gave you the container: five phases, discover, design, implement, handover, support, each with a product and an exit test.
